summary: Audited infrastructure and security configurations. Found critical authorization bypasses in Firestore rules and completely unauthenticated Cloud Functions.

findings.issue: Insecure rules for transactions, hki_valuations, and studio_assets. Only checks if businessId is not null. Any authenticated user can read/write data for ANY business, not just their own.
All Cloud Functions use https.onRequest but lack authentication middleware (e.g., verifying Firebase Auth ID tokens). They are completely public and can be invoked by anyone without authentication.
In saveTransactionAfterReview, (req as any).auth?.uid is used but will be undefined in onRequest without token verification middleware. Transactions are saved with a null UID via admin SDK.
In aiIncrementUsage, anyone can hit the public endpoint and increment AI usage counters for any businessId.
Missing CORS handling in HTTP endpoints. The frontend PWA will fail to call these endpoints from a browser origin.

ai_usage collection writes from Cloud Functions have no Firestore-level authorization checks beyond what the service account provides. Combined with unauthenticated onRequest endpoints, any caller can write to ai_usage.

recommendations: Update firestore.rules to verify user ownership of businessId, e.g., by fetching the business document: get(/databases/$(database)/documents/businesses/$(resource.data.businessId)).data.ownerId == request.auth.uid.
Change Cloud Functions from https.onRequest to https.onCall to automatically handle CORS and Firebase Auth token verification.
Alternatively, if keeping https.onRequest, add CORS middleware and Firebase Admin verifyIdToken middleware to all onRequest functions.
Add Firestore document-level security rules for ai_usage collection that verify ownership via the business document ownerId.
Consider using Firestore security rules with request.auth to tie all writes to authenticated user identity.
